title: thecophyllum palustre
intro: Thecophyllum palustre, commonly known as the bog lemming moss, is a species of liverwort, a small, non-vascular plant that belongs to the family Lepidolaenaceae. It is native to bogs and wetlands, where it grows on acidic substrates. Thecophyllum palustre is valued for its health benefits, including its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which may help to reduce stress and promote relaxation. The plant's bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, have been reported to have therapeutic actions such as antimicrobial and antifungal activities, and may also exhibit anti-proliferative and anti-apoptotic effects.
